consensus_summary: Consensus treats 'stranger' as multi-stream without a single settled primary: the vulnerable outsider (often Christ) to be welcomed in hospitality (Mt 25, OT ger laws), the believer as pilgrim/sojourner whose true home is heaven (Heb 11, 1 Pet), and the Gentile/unbeliever alienated from the covenants of promise who is brought near (Eph 2); negative or Christ-as-unrecognized uses are secondary.
book_summary: A non-citizen of God's commonwealth—one outside the covenant, drawn in, or, once in, made a stranger to the world.
consensus_core_identification: outsider/non-belonger (to community, covenant people, or the present world as pilgrim)
book_core_identification: non-citizen of God's commonwealth (covenantal outsider drawn in, or thereafter stranger to the world)
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies the Eph-2 covenantal-alien and the pilgrim-believer streams into sequential cases of one non-citizen status, while setting aside the broad ethical hospitality motif (Mt 25 independent of citizenship), Christ-as-stranger, and negative 'strange' figures that consensus often ranks as primary or common.
rationale: Minimum cores both center on lack of belonging/citizenship relative to God's people or the world; the book therefore preserves the consensus general referent. It reclassifies two separate common streams as phases of the same symbol and thereby narrows the extension away from other well-attested uses, producing real boundary disagreement without replacing the central category.
strongest_objection: Printed citations (Eph 2:12, 19) support only the outside-the-covenant and 'drawn in' half; they reverse stranger status rather than establish the believer as 'stranger to the world,' and the entry omits the widely primary hospitality reading.
